exactClaims: H0 and H1 are positive definite for the 2 by 2 pencil
the generalized eigenvalues of H1 v=x H0 v are exactly the two x atoms

effectiveMassWitness.interpretation: each value is an upper bound on the true lowest energy 0.4 and decreases toward it

intervalNoiseWitness.consequence: the interval box contains both the central spectrum with gap 0.4 and a positive spectrum with gap 0.01, so it cannot certify any lower gap above 0.01

localizingCertificate.logic: if all E>=0.5 then x<=exp(-0.5), so v^T(R H0-H1)v must be nonnegative; a strictly negative interval upper bound refutes that hypothesis
localizingCertificate.warning: feasibility of the central exact sequence at gap 0.3 is not a robust lower-gap certificate for the whole noise box

finiteWindowScaling.claim: the hidden-state effective mass remains close to 0.4 before its tiny residue is resolved, crosses over near t=46.3, and only later approaches 0.01
finiteWindowScaling.generalRule: for residue epsilon and energies Delta_hidden<Delta_visible, crossover is log(w_visible/epsilon)/(Delta_visible-Delta_hidden)

rigorousFromExactFiniteData: effective-mass and generalized-Ritz upper bounds on the lowest energy
exclusion of a proposed too-large gap by a negative localizing quadratic form
exact atom recovery when an exact flat-extension/rank hypothesis holds
notRigorousUnderNonzeroIntervalsWithoutE: a strictly positive lower bound on the energy of every state with arbitrarily small overlap
exact Hankel rank or exact finite-atomicity
absence of spectral weight below the fitted plateau
uniformity as lattice spacing tends to zero and volume and Euclidean time tend to infinity
assumptionsThatCouldChangeTheAnswer: a proved positive lower bound on spectral residue for every state in the channel
an exact finite-atomic spectrum and flat moment extension
an analytic tail bound uniform in cutoff and volume
all moments known exactly rather than a finite noisy prefix

continuumVolumeBoundary.finiteLattice: the moment test applies to the sampled finite-volume finite-cutoff transfer spectrum
continuumVolumeBoundary.missingUniformity: a Yang-Mills gap theorem needs estimates uniform in a->0, L->infinity and t_max->infinity, including overlap control near zero energy
continuumVolumeBoundary.spin23: the same moment cone can audit any reflection-positive Spin(2,3)-adjacent Euclidean channel, but group representation theory alone supplies neither reflection positivity nor the required uniform limits

decision: Finite reflection-positive samples yield rigorous positivity tests and upper bounds on the gap, and can refute a proposed gap that is too large. Exact flat data can recover a finite atomic spectrum. With any nonzero interval noise and no residue floor, a tiny positive low-energy atom can remain invisible, so a positive lower gap and its continuum-volume uniformity are not certified.
